newsitem.title: USA: Ohio Edison, Centerior to merge.
newsitem.headline: Ohio Edison, Centerior to merge.

text.p: Ohio Edison Co and Centerior Energy Corp said Monday they have signed a definitive agreement to merge in a tax-free, stock-for-stock transaction.

The new holding company is to be named FirstEnergy Corp, and would have an equity value of $4.8 billion based upon the closing prices on September 13, when Ohio Edison was at $20.75 a share and Centerior was $7.625 a share.
Under the terms of the agreement, FirstEnergy Corp will be a holding company for Ohio Edison and Centerior Energy's operating units.
The companies said they expect the transaction would positively affect earnings in the first year after the merger were completed.
Ohio Edison shareholders would receive one share of FirstEnergy's common stock for each share of Ohio Edison common stock currently held.
Centerior shareholders would receive 0.525 share of FirstEnergy's common stock for each share of Centerior common stock they currently held.
The companies said they expect savings related to the merger of about $1 billion over the first 10 years.
It is anticipated the initial annual dividend on FirstEnergy's common stock would be the same as Ohio Edison's annual dividend, which is currently $1.50 per share, the companies said.

Based on the share-exchange rate at this dividend level, Centerior shareholders would be provided about the same dividend income they now receive on Centerior shares, the companies said. Centerior's current annual dividend is $0.80 per share of common stock.
The companies said they expect to eliminate about 900 positions out of their total work force of about 11,000.

The companies said they intend to propose a plan to reduce rates for Cleveland Electric Illuminating Co and Toledo Edison customers similar to an Ohio Edison plan. The plan would call for a freeze of Cleveland Electric and Toledo rates through 2005, a rate reduction of about $300 million, or about 15 percent, in 2006, and accelerated depreciation of $2 billion in fixed costs during that period.
Cleveland Electric and Toledo Edison are operating units of Centerior Energy.
Willard Holland, president and chief executive of Ohio Edison, would become president and chief executive of FirstEnergy and chairman of its board.
Robert Farling, the chairman, president and chief executive of Centerior, would become vice chairman of FirstEnergy.
